review.summary: Round 2 reviews the whole TASK-069G branch, focusing on the fix commit after round 1. That commit changes main.py, the MCP auth tests, AI.md and TESTING.md; no other code, setting or dependency changed. create_app now imports the MCP endpoint module only when MCP is enabled. The endpoint list keeps its type through a type-checking-only import, and its local annotation is not evaluated at runtime. Two new tests close the round 1 gaps, and the AI.md and TESTING.md wording matches them. Each new test fails against its mutation. Ruff check and pyright pass; the full backend suite passes (1044 passed, 61 skipped); the new concurrent test passed six repeated runs. A production image built from a git archive of this head does not load fastmcp with MCP disabled and registers both MCP routes only with MCP enabled. Round 1's F-002 stays open for a human decision in TASK-069O, without a disposition: rejected bearer attempts are not rate-limited and share the tool capacity limiter. The local OAuth flow with Claude Code through local Caddy remains a manual check. No new findings.

prior_finding_dispositions.rationale: create_app imports the MCP endpoint module inside the MCP_ENABLED branch, and main.py has no other path to fastmcp. With MCP disabled, importing the app no longer loads fastmcp; a local probe measured about 34 MB less peak memory and about 1 s less import time than with MCP enabled. The production image built from this head confirms both states. A new test checks both states in a fresh interpreter, and it fails when the eager import is restored.

A new HTTP test seeds two Users with their own tokens and sends sequential warm-up calls, then 40 concurrent whoami calls over a file-backed SQLite database. Each call must return the calling token's own User. A mutation that makes McpBearerAuth reuse the first verified principal fails the new test, while the existing single-User test still passes.
